subject: Comments for Planning Commission members
comment: Dear Planning Commission members Ms. Jensen, Ms. Winden, Ms. Jensen, Ms. Urquiaga, Mr. Phillips, Mr. Howard, Mr. Anderson and Mr. Knudsen, Thank you for your service and commitment to helping Provo remain a wonderful place to live. I want to comment on the first agenda item tonight - Provo City Council Office requests an ordinance amendment to establish the Critical Hillside (CH) Overlay Zone to provide development standards to help protect the sensitive hillside areas of Provo City’s east bench. Citywide Impact. Brandon Larsen [redacted-phone] [redacted-email] PLOTA20200077 George Handley and others have been working hard to get this overlay document in place. We have referred to it as the Foothills Protection Ordinance for many months. We are grateful to all who have worked to make this document a reality. I read an initial draft of the document a few days ago. I sent comments and concerns, gathered from several others and myself, to George and to Bill Peperone. I didn't get answers to some of my questions but I support the document and the strength it will have to protect the foothills of Provo. In the draft was this item: 14.33A.140 A development that would produce 250 vehicle trips per day shall have at least 2 points of ingress or egress. All developments shall be connected to the City's street system at (2) different access locations. I heard this morning that the engineering department wanted this item removed so I'm not sure it's in the current document. Bill Peperone is concerned that 2 accesses just carves out more of the mountain which is a greater environmental impact. I support his suggestion to take out the two points of access but I still think it's important to have wording regarding the number of vehicle trips per day or wording that will limit the number of dwellings and size of a development. There MUST be wording about limiting the impact any development has. The zoning for that area will help as well but only if the zoning designation isn't changed so additional wording restricting how many vehicle trips (as a standard) in a development will be helpful. While I would love to see NO development in the foothills, I understand there needs to be a compromise since people own property and have property rights. I believe this document limits and discourages further development - please review it to make sure that it does and approve it so we can protect the foothills for now and future generations to enjoy. Thank you - Kaye Nelson [redacted-phone] -- Kaye Nelson "There's no place like home."

subject: Please pass the Critical Foothill Overlay with the strength to limit development of our beautiful
comment: foothills... Importance: High Dear Provo Planning Commission... Thank you for your good work on our City’s behalf. I’m delighted you are working on protecting one of our most precious resources–our foothills! I encourage you to strengthen and approve the Provo “Critical Foothill Overlay” that you will be reviewing tonight. This Overlay should help to limit development, restrict roads and traffic, require greatly reduced housing density and protect our greenspace. Property rights are important, and need to be respected. And, not all property is created equal. Development that happens in the foothills is a shared responsibility with the entire city of Provo. Because of its visible nature, we all look at it and we all have a common right to insist that it be done in a way that future generations will admire and appreciate. Please, please, send a document to the City Council that gives maximum protection to our beautiful foothills and its sensitive environment. Enable this Overlay to encourage minimal and unobtrusive development. With gratitude, Craig Christensen Sherwood Hills Neighborhood

subject: Critical Hills Overlay
comment: Dear Planning Commission Members, First of all, thank you so much for continuing to work on behalf of all the citizens of Provo during this very tumultuous time in our history. We appreciate all your work on this project to date. Please stay safe and healthy. My husband and I are very grateful that you are forward thinking and want to protect the foothills of Provo. By crafting this document with the utmost protection to the foothills you will be preserving the foothills for generations to come. Please make sure that there is a limit to development in the foothills to safeguard the beauty of our natural resources and environment. Please make this document as strong as possible to ensure that development cannot expand and find loopholes to extend their development. I have lived in northeast Provo for 37 years and know that there are uncharted natural springs that pop up in “wet” years that can and have undermined home foundations causing those homes to be unsafe. They have now been torn down and those lots have been deemed unbuildable. In the past, there was also a problem with Manning canyon shale that slipped during “wet” years and undermined foundations of homes that had to be torn down or that sustained thousands of dollars in repairs. Does this developer have to put up a bond so that what happened in Eagle Mountain does not happen here in Provo? Thank you very much, Dr. Lynn M. Gaufin and Cynthia Gaufin

subject: For the Planning Commission Members about the Foothill Preservation Ordinance
comment: Dear Planning Commission Members I am so grateful that you are working on an ordinance for the preservation of the Foothills of Provo. The effort this is taking will have a profound affect in years to come on land that we cannot take back, once it is developed. I am concerned about the changes in the draft of the Foothills Preservation Ordinance. I understand that you are deleting the trips per day each household makes in a development. I urge you to put back the language of the ordinance that limits how many trips a day each household can do. I also would ask that a second road to a culdesac not be made to preserve as much of this pristine land as possible. A second road will also encourage further development. The work you are doing on this document will help development not get out of control, and will preserve what is beautiful and natural. I am also asking you to limit further development beyond the proposed Terra Development in the Provo foothills. Finally, please keep the strong language in the document that will preserve and protect Provo's foothills. Sincerely, Susan Christensen

subject: Please support the foothills protection ordinance
comment: Hello, I am writing to you to thank you for your work in protecting the foothills of Provo and doing such important work of taking the crucial steps needed to protect such precious land. I ask you approve the ordinance in order for it to pass and be implemented quickly as development is encroaching upon these hillsides. I ask that you please include wording to limit the number of trips per day in a development to limit the number of units that can be built. I also ask that you do everything in your power to make sure this document provides the utmost protection over this land. It is so important that you do so, for those of us living now and all those to come after us in Provo and those who come from all over the world to visit our precious outdoors. I ask that you make sure this document limits both development and the impact of development in these hills. Please make sure it limits what kind of development can happen and limits any development in the future. We must safeguard our natural resources and the beauty that makes Provo so special. Please don’t take out what makes this document strong, binding, or powerful. It must be strict and specific. Thank you so much for all of your hard work and time. I hope you are all staying safe and healthy in this time. Hunter Gibson
